issues.display_title: Issue #1008: perf(map): hover highlight falls seconds behind the cursor on large floor plans (setFilter reloads the whole floor-plan source)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #981 / #982. On the visitor map the room highlight trails the cursor by seconds and keeps replaying rooms after the cursor has stopped. Reported in a screen recording on production /v/UkZnTKwv (Square One Mall V6 (Demo), building Default, Level 2).

Measured

  • Screen recording, frame by frame: while the cursor keeps moving the lag grows from ~80–450 ms to ~2 s. The cursor stops at 9.25 s; the highlight keeps moving through the rooms it passed until 10.75 s.
  • Production, headless Chrome on the GPU (.playwright-mcp/demo/hover-lag/probe-queue.mjs), Level 2 at zoom 18: source floorplan holds 12,043 features in 16 tiles.
    • One hover change → 16 tile reloads, ~0.9 s until all have landed.
    • 6 s continuous sweep → 60 hover changes → 960 tile reloads; hover-to-paint median 17.7 s, max 34.7 s; the queue drains 35 s after the cursor stops; frame median 50 ms while moving.

Cause (checked in code)

  1. applyHighlight (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts:122) moves the hover with map.setFilter on the four highlight layers. Those layers share source floorplan with the whole model.
  2. In maplibre 5.24, Style.setFilter → _updateLayer marks the layer's source for reload, so every hover change re-parses every tile of floorplan in the worker, for every layer, not only the highlight.
  3. Reloads are not coalesced (GeoJSONSource.loadTile → worker _reloadLoadedTile parses each request). Crossing rooms faster than one full re-parse builds a queue, and the highlight replays it.
  4. Why #982 missed it: its probe timed the first render after setFilter, which still draws the old tiles, and moved the cursor every 200 ms, which never builds a queue.

The same path serves: area hover on the visitor map (usePreviewSelectionLayers), marker-pill hover (PreviewOverlay handleObjectMarkerHover), area and marker hover on the Editor Map tab (Editor3DMapView), Information-row hover (infoHoverIds), and selection (applySelection, one full reload per click).

Scope

  • Give the hover highlight layers their own small GeoJSON source that holds only the hovered features. A hover change becomes a setData on that source instead of a setFilter on floorplan. Same layers, same paint, same matching (area by id; flat wall line by id; 3D wall strips by wallId / closedAreaId), so the highlight looks the same.
  • Do the same for the selection layers (applySelection).
  • Keep the highlight correct when the floor-plan data changes underneath it (level switch, editor edits), after a base-style reload, and on a 2D/3D mode switch.
  • Not in scope: the 7–8 queryRenderedFeatures per mousemove from the delegated layer listeners (~12 ms per move measured). Follow up separately if it still shows once the queue is gone.
  • No new dependency.

Acceptance criteria

  • Same probe, same project: a hover change reloads no floorplan tile, and a 6 s sweep leaves no queue (the highlight settles within a few frames of the cursor stopping).
  • The highlight looks unchanged: area in 3D and flat, a Closed room lights its walls, marker-pill and Information-row hover still highlight, selection still highlights.
  • Editor Map tab hover still works; editor view mode still suppresses the highlight.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo per the demo convention.

RESULT

Fix

e93c5f6 perf(map): move the hover highlight and selection off the model source — PR #1009

  • The hover highlight and selection layers now draw from sources of their own, floorplan-highlight and floorplan-selected. Each holds copies of only the features it lights up, tagged hl with the layer that paints them (src/lib/map/layer-definitions.ts).
  • applyHighlight / applySelection (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts) cut those copies from the model with the same matching the filters used, then push them with setData: area by id, flat wall line by id, 3D wall strips by wallId / closedAreaId, and for selection any feature by id. Calling either again with the same ids pushes nothing.
  • Every model push re-cuts both overlays, so they stay correct across a level switch, an editor edit, a base-style reload and a 2D/3D switch.
  • No setFilter is left in the hover or selection path, no new dependency, no Go API change.

Verification

Same probe as the report (.playwright-mcp/demo/hover-lag/probe-queue.mjs), headless Chrome on the GPU, Square One /v/UkZnTKwv, building Default, Level 2, zoom 18:

development (:6060) this branch (:6066)
floorplan tile reloads caused by hover 784 0
hover → highlight painted, median 13.6 s 130 ms
hover → highlight painted, max 27.7 s 224 ms
queue drains after the cursor stops 28.3 s 36 ms
reloads in flight at once 645 16 (the highlight source's own tiles, ~44 ms each)
  • Visitor map (visual-check.mjs): hovering a Closed room copies the room plus its 50 shell wall strips; hovering an open room copies the room only; hovering the Aritzia marker pill highlights its room. Preview passes no selection ids, so the selection source stays empty there, as before.
  • Editor Map tab (editor-check.mjs, scratch copy, deleted afterwards): the hover lands in 76 ms (room plus 18 wall strips); a click selects it in 63 ms; moving off clears the hover and keeps the selection (blue). Zero setFilter calls on highlight or selection layers.
  • Unit tests (useFloorPlanLayer.highlight.test.tsx):
    • every overlay layer draws from an overlay source;
    • a hover copies only the room and its sealing walls, with no filter and no model push;
    • the same room again pushes nothing;
    • a model change re-cuts the hover;
    • a 3D → flat switch re-tags it;
    • a selection lands on the selection source only.
  • pnpm test 249 files / 2,357 passed, pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1008/video-1008-hover-highlight.mp4 (55 s, 1920x1080, 60 fps, page loads cut; full take video-1008-hover-highlight-raw.mp4). The same camera and the same 5 s sweep across 12 linked shops run on development and then on the fix; a HUD shows the tile reloads queued for the highlight's source. After the cursor stops, development keeps walking the highlight through the passed rooms (611 reloads queued) and settles 24.8 s later; the fix settles in 137 ms.

Not addressed

  • The delegated layer listeners still run 7–8 queryRenderedFeatures per mousemove (~10 ms per move measured).
  • A hover change still reloads every in-view tile of the small highlight source (16 × ~44 ms). That no longer queues, but it is what the remaining ~130 ms is made of.

issues.display_title: Issue #1013: fix(map): wall edges look pixelized — the map canvas has no antialiasing
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Feedback from Alin, comparing our Square One map with the Mappedin one: "to me these 2 maps do not look the same, our map is not even close to the mappedin map regarding lines, our are very pixelized". Mappedin's wall edges are smooth; ours are stair-stepped.

Cause (checked in code and in the browser)

  • The only maplibre map constructor (src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx:130) passes no canvasContextAttributes.
  • maplibre 5.24 defaults to antialias: false, so the WebGL canvas has no MSAA (gl.getParameter(gl.SAMPLES) = 0).
  • 3D wall extrusions are plain triangles, so with no MSAA every wall edge is aliased. Wall caps also show dark speckles along the seam. (Flat fill layers draw their own antialiased outline, which is why the basemap looks fine.)

Measured

Visitor map /v/UkZnTKwv, building Default, Level 2, zoom 19.6, pitch 50, headless Chrome on the GPU at DPR 1. Same camera both ways; MSAA forced on through the WebGL context attributes.

MSAA off (ships today) MSAA on
samples 0 4
wall edges stair-stepped, dark speckles on the cap seam smooth
render per frame (2 runs) 27.8 / 24.7 ms 26.5 / 27.0 ms

The frame-cost difference is within run-to-run noise.

Scope

  • Create the map with canvasContextAttributes: { antialias: true } in MapLibreCore. Every map goes through it: the visitor map / embed, the editor Map tab, the new-project flow and the add-panorama location modal.
  • Not in scope: styling the walls closer to Mappedin (thinner walls, no dark cap/base bands, soft shading). That is a separate design question.
  • No new dependency.

Acceptance criteria

  • On the reported project, the visitor map's WebGL context reports antialias with samples > 0, and wall edges are smooth at the same camera where they were stair-stepped before (before/after screenshots).
  • Render cost per frame on Square One Level 2 is no worse beyond noise.
  • Editor Map tab and the new-project flow map still render.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Fix

9912682 fix(map): antialias the map canvas so wall edges are smooth — PR #1014

  • MapLibreCore (src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx) now creates the map with canvasContextAttributes: { antialias: true }.
  • maplibre's default gives a canvas without MSAA, and the 3D wall extrusions have no antialiasing of their own. The flag turns MSAA on for every map: the visitor map / embed, the editor Map tab, the new-project dialog and the add-panorama location modal.
  • WebGL does not expose a sample count; the browser picks it (4 in Chrome). Kept at that after measuring 8x (below).
  • No new dependency, no Go API change.

Verification

Visitor map /v/UkZnTKwv (Square One, Default, Level 2, zoom 19.6, pitch 50), headless Chrome on the GPU at DPR 1, development (:6060) vs this branch (:6066), same camera:

development this branch
WebGL antialias / samples false / 0 true / 4
wall edges stair-stepped, dark speckles on the cap seam smooth
render per frame (2 runs) 26.0 / 22.9 ms 26.0 / 23.4 ms
  • 4x vs 8x (8x forced with --webgl-msaa-sample-count=8, GPU max 8): render per frame 45.3 / 42.5 / 41.3 ms at 4x vs 46.0 / 40.5 / 43.3 ms at 8x. The 4x-magnified edge is barely different. WebGL2 only guarantees 4 samples, and 8x roughly doubles the multisample buffer.
  • Editor Map tab (scratch copy, deleted afterwards): renders with antialias true / 4 samples; hovering and clicking a room still highlight and select it.
  • New-project dialog (stopped before creating anything): its location map renders with antialias true / 4 samples.
  • pnpm test 251 files / 2,368 passed, pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.
  • Screenshots: .playwright-mcp/screenshot/1013-*.
  • Demo recorder (real Chrome on Xvfb, ANGLE Vulkan on the Tesla P4, 1920x1080), same camera: render per frame 14.2 ms before, 16.0 ms after. The headless probe measured no difference; on this setup MSAA costs about 1.8 ms a frame, still well under a 60 fps budget.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1013/video-1013-map-antialias.mp4 (28 s, 1920x1080, 60 fps; page loads and camera turns cut). The same wall edge on development and on the fix, outlined on the map and shown 4× nearest-neighbour, ending side by side with the HUD reading the WebGL context's antialias and sample count. Full take: video-1013-map-antialias-raw.mp4.

Not addressed

  • Wall styling is still not Mappedin's: our walls are thicker, have dark cap/base bands and no soft shading. That is a design question, not aliasing.

issues.display_title: Issue #1018: feat(editor): standalone Area color — toolbar picker, shown in the editor, map and viewers (#1016)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1018-area-color.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1016 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-09-15-standalone-area-color/prd.md on product-docs). This task is the Area color part only (R1–R16). Room wall removal and Closed Room opacity (R17–R23) wait on the open questions posted on #1016.

Current state (checked in code, development 7050448)

  • Toolbar: the Area toolbar holds only Delete area and Convert to room (SelectionToolbars.tsx:465-470); its comment deliberately rules out the Closed colour control.
  • Engine: the colour command refuses an Area — setAreaColor resolves the room through areaMetaKey, which returns null for a manual room (commands.ts:70-72).
  • Persistence mostly exists: bridge.ts already reads and writes color for manual areas (levelToModel :168/:188, modelToLevel metaOf :298/:319). AreaLayer.color is documented as Closed-only (useMapStore.types.ts:64-68), and a stored closed migrated off an Area also clears its colour (bridge.ts:188).
  • 2D canvas: an Area always draws a C.sel fill (8 %, 18 % selected) with a dashed C.hot/C.sel outline (draw.ts:302-313).
  • Editor 3D pane: rooms and Areas are coloured from ctx.areaColors[i], which the host fills from closedRoomColors — Closed rooms only (FloorplanEditor.tsx:638, closedRoom.ts:339).
  • Map: canvasDataToGeoJson sets areaColor only for type === "closed" (geojson-utils.ts:1275); every other area gets the cream slab AREA_COLOR_EXPR and AREA_LINE_COLOR. Every viewer surface goes through this one builder via useFloorPlanLayer: the editor Map tab, /preview/[projectId], /v/[key], and /embed/[key] (which renders the /v page).

Scope

  • Area toolbar: a colour input beside Delete area / Convert to room, for one selected standalone Area only. Copy from the PRD: label "Color", aria-label "Area color", tooltip "Change area color".
  • Engine: an Area colour command addressed by manualIndex (not the ctx.rooms position), with the Closed colour's gesture pattern: live 2D repaint while the picker is dragged, one undo step and one store sync per gesture.
  • Persist as AreaLayer.color on the Area (manual: true); update the field's doc comment. canvasData reaches the Go API as an opaque string — no API contract change.
  • Render the colour on the Area's fill and outline (outline = darker companion via outlineFor, the rule shapes and Closed walls already use):
    • 2D canvas — semi-transparent like the other fills, selection and hover still readable;
    • editor 3D pane;
    • map GeoJSON → Map tab, preview, published and embed views.
  • Uncolored Areas render exactly as today (no colour key on the feature, no entry in the colour map).
  • Convert to room keeps working for a coloured Area; the Area colour does not travel to the Room (Room colour exists only for Closed).
  • Out of scope: Room colour, Shape colour, room type / Closed behaviour / logo on Areas, routing and search, Room wall removal and Closed Room opacity (R17–R23).

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting one standalone Area shows the colour control in the Area toolbar; selecting a Room or a Shape shows no new control.
  • Changing the colour updates the Area fill and outline immediately in the 2D canvas and the editor 3D pane.
  • One picker gesture = one undo step; Ctrl+Z brings back the previous colour (or the default style).
  • The colour persists after save and reload.
  • The colour shows in the Map tab, preview, published and embed views.
  • Labels and markers on or next to a coloured Area stay readable.
  • Uncolored Areas look unchanged on every surface.
  • Closed Room colour and Shape colour behave as before.
  • A coloured Area converts to a Room, and the Room follows the existing Room rules.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; demo per the demo convention on a scratch project.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/1018-standalone-area-color: commit 27f7e8e, PR #1021 → development (merge 89bec99) · released via PR #1025 → main (003562e).

  • Toolbar: Color picker for one selected standalone Area (label "Color", aria-label "Area color", tooltip "Change area color") — SelectionToolbars.tsx.
  • Engine: beginManualAreaColorEdit / setManualAreaColor — commands.ts, index.ts.
    • Addressed by the manualAreas index; the colour is stored on model.areaMeta under m:<id>.
    • Shares the Closed colour gesture, so one picker drag is one undo step and one sync.
  • Rendering:
    • 2D fill at 35 % with a darker dashed outline — draw.ts;
    • editor 3D pane volume — scene3d.ts;
    • map areaColor + areaLineColor, which reaches the Map tab, preview, published and embed views — geojson-utils.ts, layer-definitions.ts.
  • Persistence: AreaLayer.color on the Area (doc updated in useMapStore.types.ts).
    • Convert to room does not carry the colour.
    • Uncoloured Areas are unchanged.
  • Tests: area-color.test.ts, SelectionToolbars.areaColor.test.tsx, geojson-area-color.test.ts (mutation checks 4/4). Full suite 254 files green; lint and tsc clean.
  • Browser check (GPU, Square One scratch copy): the colour persists after autosave + reload and shows on the Map tab.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1018/video-1018-area-color.mp4.
  • Found while demoing: a pre-existing autosave race, filed as #1024.

issues.display_title: Issue #1019: feat(editor): Closed Room opacity — stepped control, shown in the editor, map and viewers (#1016)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1019-closed-opacity.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1016 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-09-15-standalone-area-color/prd.md on product-docs), Closed Room opacity (R20–R22). Decisions from the answers to the questions on #1016 (2026-09-15):

  • a Closed Room stays a full-height solid block, and the opacity applies to that block;
  • the default is fully opaque — today's look.

Related: Area color #1018; wall removal and room outlines #1020.

Current state (checked in code, development 7050448)

  • No room opacity anywhere. The only opacity setting in the editor is the backdrop image.
  • Toolbar: a Closed Room has Color and Logo controls (SelectionToolbars.tsx:325-440). Color is written through setAreaColor with one undo step and one store sync per picker gesture (commands.ts:150-190).
  • 2D canvas: the Closed shell is filled at a fixed 35 % alpha (draw.ts:102-112).
  • Editor 3D pane: room meshes use an opaque MeshBasicMaterial in ctx.areaColors[i] (scene3d.ts:195-205).
  • Map: every area fill uses fill-opacity: 0.85 (flat), and the active-level extrusion layer uses fill-extrusion-opacity: 0.95 (3D) (layer-definitions.ts).
  • Map library limit: fill-extrusion-opacity applies to a whole layer — it is not data-driven — and the alpha in fill-extrusion-color is ignored (MapLibre style-spec 24.8.5). The flat fill-opacity is data-driven.

Scope

  • Data: AreaLayer.opacity, Closed rooms only, following the color rule: ignored for other types, kept so switching back to Closed restores it, absent = fully opaque. canvasData reaches the Go API as an opaque string — no API contract change.
  • Toolbar (Closed controls): a stepped opacity control with 5 steps — 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 % — defaulting to 100 %. Copy from the PRD: label "Opacity", aria-label "Room opacity", tooltip "Adjust room opacity". One undo step per gesture, like Color.
  • Fill only: the room outline and the Closed-room logo stay fully visible.
  • Render:
    • 2D canvas: the Closed fill alpha scales with the opacity;
    • editor 3D pane: the Closed room mesh is transparent at the opacity;
    • map, flat: fill-opacity read from the feature;
    • map, 3D: one Closed-room extrusion layer per step, filtered on the step. The 100 % step keeps today's look, and the lower-level ghost layer is unchanged.
  • Out of scope:
    • hiding walls and drawing room outlines, plus that task's per-project opt-in (#1020). The opacity default changes nothing on existing projects, so opacity itself needs no opt-in.
    • routing, search, room classification.

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting one Closed Room shows the Opacity control; other room types, Areas and Shapes do not.
  • Changing the step updates the Closed Room fill immediately in the 2D canvas and the editor 3D pane; the outline and logo stay visible at every step.
  • One gesture = one undo step.
  • The opacity persists after save and reload, and survives switching the type away from Closed and back.
  • The Map tab, preview, published and embed views show the same opacity, flat and 3D (stacked levels included).
  • Existing Closed Rooms (no opacity stored) look exactly as today.
  • Hover and selection highlight still work on a see-through Closed Room.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; demo per the demo convention on a scratch project.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/1019-closed-room-opacity: commit 4ccef08, PR #1022 → development (merge a5afe6c) · released via PR #1025 → main (003562e).

  • Toolbar: Closed room Opacity slider, 5 steps (20–100 %), default 100 %, so existing rooms are unchanged. It rides the colour gesture.
  • Data: AreaLayer.opacity, Closed rooms only, kept across type changes; carried on model.areaMeta and through the bridge.
  • Rendering:
    • 2D: the Closed fill alpha scales; walls and logo keep full strength.
    • Editor 3D pane: the room mesh is transparent.
    • Map: the feature carries areaOpacity; the flat layer scales fill-opacity.
    • Map 3D: one extrusion layer per step, because fill-extrusion-opacity is per layer in MapLibre. Hover, click and marquee listen to all of them (AREA_EXTRUSION_LAYERS).
  • Files:
    • closedRoom.ts (closedRoomOpacity, steps);
    • bridge.ts, types.ts, model-sync.ts, commands.ts, index.ts, context.ts, draw.ts, scene3d.ts;
    • geojson-utils.ts, layer-definitions.ts, Editor3DMapView.tsx, usePreviewSelectionLayers.ts, useMapSelect.ts;
    • SelectionToolbars.tsx, useMapStore.types.ts.
  • Tests: 4 new files (mutation checks 6/6); the areaMeta seed tests now expect opacity: null. Full suite 258 files green; lint and tsc clean.
  • Browser check (GPU, Square One scratch copy):
    • opacity 0.4 saved;
    • plan and pane repaint;
    • Walmart shows see-through on the Map tab;
    • no MapLibre layer errors.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1019/video-1019-closed-opacity.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1020: feat(map): opt-in room outlines — hide the walls of Closed Rooms and open-to-below areas (#1016)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1020-room-outlines.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1016 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-09-15-standalone-area-color/prd.md on product-docs), room wall removal and outlines (R17–R19, R21, R23).

Decisions (answers to the questions on #1016, 2026-09-15)

  1. "Open Rooms" means the Open type, open-to-below. Rooms of type Room and Hallway keep their walls.
  2. Surfaces: the editor 2D canvas keeps its walls, because walls are drawn and edited there. The change applies to the map (editor Map tab, preview, published, embed) and to the editor 3D pane.
  3. Closed Room shape: a Closed Room stays a full-height solid block, and the opacity from #1019 applies to it. Doors and windows on a Closed Room are hidden.
  4. Opacity default: fully opaque (#1019).
  5. Opt-in per project: existing projects render exactly as today until the setting is turned on.

Current state (checked in code, development 7050448)

  • Map, Closed Rooms:
    • bounding walls are tinted in the room colour and sealed, with no door or window cut (closedWallOwners + sealed, geojson-utils.ts:1151-1180);
    • a door on the boundary gets no marker (object-markers.ts:126-132);
    • the shell extrudes to roof height (closedRoomRoofOffset, geojson-utils.ts:1263).
  • Map, open-to-below: no slab and no outline is emitted (geojson-utils.ts:1256); its walls render normally.
  • Area outline today: the flat fp-area-line layer, 1 px AREA_LINE_COLOR. The 3D layers draw no outline.
  • Editor 3D pane: there is no Closed treatment. Every wall is built with its door/window openings cut (scene3d.ts:231-260), and rooms extrude to rm.height.
  • Precedent for a project setting: CanvasData.showPanoConnections (#544).
    • toggled in EditFileModal.tsx ("Show connection lines on live", :405-411);
    • absent = default;
    • viewers read it straight from canvasData.

Scope

  • Project setting: CanvasData.roomOutlines?: boolean (name open), absent = off. A checkbox in EditFileModal next to the connection-lines setting. canvasData reaches the Go API as an opaque string — no API contract change.
  • When ON — on the map (Map tab, preview, published, embed) and in the editor 3D pane:
    • walls bounding a Closed Room or an open-to-below area are not drawn. A wall that also bounds a Room or Hallway stays, so that room keeps its wall.
    • Closed Room: the full-height solid block as today (with the #1019 opacity), plus a perimeter outline in a darker companion of its colour (outlineFor, palette.ts:32), visible at every opacity step.
    • open-to-below: still no floor, with an outline around the void.
    • Outlines are distinct enough to separate adjacent rooms without becoming a heavy divider. MapLibre line layers lie on the ground plane, so in 3D the outline needs a thin extruded perimeter band at level height (like the wall cap).
    • Doors and windows on a Closed Room's boundary are hidden. The map already does this; the editor 3D pane must stop cutting and drawing them.
    • The hover and selection highlight of a Closed Room still works with its walls hidden. Today it takes the shell walls via closedAreaId.
  • When OFF: every surface renders exactly as today.
  • Editor 2D canvas: unchanged — walls, doors and windows stay visible and editable.
  • Out of scope: routing, search, room classification; Area color (#1018); the opacity control (#1019).

Acceptance criteria

  • The new project setting is in the Edit File modal, off by default; existing projects look unchanged until it is turned on.
  • Setting on: a Closed Room shows no walls — a full-height block with a visible outline at every opacity step.
  • Setting on: an open-to-below area shows no walls, and shows an outline.
  • Walls shared with a Room or Hallway stay; Room and Hallway walls are unaffected.
  • Adjacent Closed Rooms stay distinguishable by their outlines.
  • Doors and windows on a Closed Room boundary are not shown on the map or in the editor 3D pane, and are still present and editable in the 2D canvas.
  • The same treatment shows in the Map tab, preview, published and embed views (flat and 3D, stacked levels included) and in the editor 3D pane.
  • Hover and selection highlight of a Closed Room still work with the setting on.
  • The setting persists after save and reload; turning it off restores today's rendering.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; demo per the demo convention on a scratch project.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/1020-room-outlines: commit 3df3c14, PR #1023 → development (merge 8c11e9f) · released via PR #1025 → main (003562e).

  • Project setting: CanvasData.roomOutlines, an Edit File Info checkbox "Outline Closed and Open rooms instead of walls", off by default (opt-in per project) — EditFileModal.tsx.
  • When on — map (Map tab, preview, published, embed) and editor 3D pane:
    • Closed-room and open-to-below walls are hidden. A wall shared with a Room or Hallway stays: outlineHiddenSegments decides per segment on the map, outlineWalls works off Room.wallIdx in the pane.
    • Closed rooms stay full-height blocks with a roof-edge rim in a darker companion colour; open-to-below areas get a floor-level rim. The flat view draws lines; 3D draws thin extruded bands.
    • Pane: the Closed block is full height with an outline, and a Closed room's walls are not cut for doors or windows.
  • When off: every surface renders as before. The 2D plan is always unchanged.
  • Files: closedRoom.ts, geojson-utils.ts, layer-definitions.ts, scene3d.ts, index.ts, context.ts, FloorplanEditor.tsx, EditFileModal.tsx, useMapStore.types.ts.
  • Tests: room-outlines, geojson-room-outlines, EditFileModal.roomOutlines (mutation checks 7/7). Full suite 261 files green; lint and tsc clean.
  • Browser check (GPU): the setting saves, pane walls are hidden, no layer errors.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1020/video-1020-room-outlines.mp4.
  • Note: the 3D rim is thin (12 cm × 5 cm). Outline contrast is PRD Open Question 1 and can be thickened on request.
